title: Lior and the Choir Anew
premise: Cyrus Amberdale keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in stolen memories, and hides their own gift: they can take a memory by touch. When the crown declares the Hunt, branding memory-thieves as traitors to a kingdom that is quietly being unmade, Cyrus flees with Lior, a choirless singer whose voice can open doors between what-is and what-was. Together they seek the Last Door out of a country that no longer exists on any map, pursued by the King's Tuner, who once loved Lior and now hunts them. In the end Cyrus must give up every memory they have ever stolen—including their own name—to sing Lior through the Door, choosing love over survival; Lior returns for them anyway, and what steps back into the world is someone new, remembered only by each other.
about_author: A. M. Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters people never sent. They write fantasy about the things we trade away to stay alive.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Thefts
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. We meet the Vellum Guild's counting house, where memories are weighed like coin, and Cyrus's careful double-books hiding the memories they've kept instead of sold. A client arrives wanting to forget her dead son—and Cyrus refuses the fee. Emotional beat: quiet complicity cracking into conscience.

chapters.title: A Voice With No Choir
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior sings at a funeral for hire, voice able to make mourners remember better days that never happened. Afterward, guildmaster Ondrey offers Lior a dangerous commission: sing a door open in the palace vaults. Emotional beat: longing for belonging, tempted by purpose.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Criers announce the Hunt: all gifted with memory-taking are enemies of the crown, to be 'tuned'—emptied. Guild members begin vanishing overnight. Ondrey burns half the ledgers and gives Cyrus the true one to carry. Emotional beat: dread arriving as bureaucracy.

chapters.title: What the Vault Kept
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The palace job goes wrong: behind the vault door is not treasure but a country—a preserved slice of the old kingdom, pre-Hunt, singing faintly. Guards catch them; Lior escapes through a door only they can hear. Emotional beat: awe curdling into terror.

chapters.title: Runners in the Ash Market
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus finds Lior bleeding in the ash market, recognizes the gift-scent on them, and makes a thief's bargain: mutual silence, mutual escape. The Tuner's hounds pass close enough to touch. Emotional beat: two strangers choosing each other out of necessity.

chapters.title: The Tuner
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV (Serah Vane). The King's Tuner interrogates a captured guild member and we learn her method and her wound: she was Lior's first love, emptied herself to serve the crown, and remembers loving Lior without remembering why. Emotional beat: chilling devotion built on a hole.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. On the road north, Cyrus teaches Lior how hunted people move; Lior catches Cyrus taking a memory from a dying farmer—not stealing, but keeping it safe. First real fight. Emotional beat: intimacy through friction.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. They cross a border that no map admits exists; villages here remember a different king, different songs. An innkeeper feeds them free because 'singers are owed.' Lior realizes the old country survives wherever its songs do. Emotional beat: grief and wonder braided together.

chapters.title: Price Tags
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus confesses the ledger's secret column: names of everyone whose memories they hold, including one entry labeled only 'C.A.'—a memory Cyrus took from themselves long ago. Lior demands to know what it holds. Cyrus doesn't know anymore. Emotional beat: vulnerability as exposure.

chapters.title: The Choir of the Hollowed
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. They find a hidden settlement of the tuned—people emptied by the crown, humming fragments of lives they can't recall. Among them, Serah's first victim: Lior's old music teacher. Emotional beat: horror made tender; the cost of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: What Serah Remembers
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah tracks them but hesitates at the settlement's edge, hearing a song she knows without knowing it. Flashbacks in fragments: rain, a duet, a promise. She reports a false location to her superiors. Emotional beat: duty beginning to fracture.

chapters.title: The Bridge of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. To cross the river into the deep old-country, someone must pay the bridge-warden in years of memory. Cyrus pays without telling Lior, losing whole seasons—their mother's face goes gray in their mind. Emotional beat: love as silent expenditure.

chapters.title: Doorsong
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior learns the full nature of their gift from a door-wight: singers don't open doors, they remember places so hard the place remembers itself. But every doorsong erases one of the singer's own memories. Emotional beat: understanding the bill coming due.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Reliquary
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The Tuner's second team, not Serah, corners them in a reliquary of confiscated gifts. Cyrus takes a soldier's entire childhood to stop him—and feels it settle in them like a stone. Lior sees what Cyrus is becoming. Emotional beat: rescue that costs innocence.

chapters.title: The Argument in the Snow
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Lior says they should split up: Cyrus is becoming a hoard, Lior is becoming a key, and both are being spent. Cyrus refuses. The fight turns into a confession neither planned. Emotional beat: love named aloud for the first time, at the worst moment.

chapters.title: Serah's Choice
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Ordered to execute the hollowed settlement as collaborators, Serah instead opens the cages and burns her own tuning instruments. She sends word to Lior: the Last Door is real, and the crown already knows where it stands. Emotional beat: treason as an act of remembering.

chapters.title: The March of the Unwritten
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The hollowed join their march to the Door, a slow procession of people carrying nothing but hummed fragments. Crown riders shadow them, waiting for orders. Cyrus begins giving memories back to their owners along the road, emptying the ledger. Emotional beat: restitution as redemption.

chapters.title: The Last Door
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. They reach the Door: a cathedral-sized threshold standing in a field of unmown grass, guarded by the wight and by soldiers under orders to hold it shut until the Tuner arrives. Lior must sing it open while Cyrus buys time. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: Duet for a Dying Country
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The battle at the Door. Serah arrives and, instead of tuning Lior, joins the song—the three voices together are what the Door requires. The old country begins to pour through, and the wight warns: the singer who opens it cannot pass carrying anything, not even themselves. Emotional beat: climax as harmony under fire.

chapters.title: The Emptying of Cyrus Amberdale
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus sings Lior through, then pays the toll: every stolen memory returned, every kept memory surrendered, down to their own name. They push Lior fully across as the Door narrows. Final line of self they lose is Lior's face. Emotional beat: sacrifice complete, identity dissolved.

chapters.title: On the Other Side of the Song
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior wakes in the old country, whole, in a kingdom that remembers its songs—but Cyrus did not come through. Refusing the ending, Lior does the forbidden thing: sings the Door from the far side, paying with their own past, holding onto one thing only—the sound of Cyrus saying their name. Emotional beat: love refusing arithmetic.

chapters.title: Choir Anew
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Someone steps out of the Door with no name and no past, and Lior meets them with the only memory left: theirs. They begin again—two people building a self from a single shared recollection, while behind them the hollowed arrive through the reopened Door, humming. Epilogue beat: identity not found but chosen, sung into being together.
